proxy_language: Proto-Uralic (late reconstruction, Sammallahti/Janhunen/Aikio tradition), as a speculative stand-in for the languages of Final Palaeolithic and Early Mesolithic foragers of the Russian Plain, Volga and Urals
proxy_rationale: The Final Palaeolithic and Early Mesolithic archaeological cultures of the Russian Plain and Urals (Zhokhov-adjacent, Butovo, Volga-Oka, Kama, Trans-Ural Mesolithic) have no direct linguistic record. Proto-Uralic is the best-defended reconstructed language family anchored in the Volga-Kama-Urals forest zone, though it is usually dated to the Neolithic or later (c. 5000-3000 BCE), thousands of years after these foragers. The link is weak: these foragers could have spoken languages now extinct, Uralic precursors, or unrelated Palaeo-European or Siberian languages. Proto-Uralic roots for fauna, fishing and forest life are used as the most defensible phonological and morphological model for a hunter-fisher-gatherer lexicon of this region.
phonology: Proto-Uralic reconstruction (Sammallahti 1988; Aikio 2022). Consonants: *p *t *k *c *c' *s *s' *m *n *n' *n-velar *w *l *l' *r *j *d *d' *x. Vowels: *a *e *i *u *o *ä *ü *ə (reduced vowel in non-initial syllables, often written *e or *i). First-syllable vowels are a fuller set; non-initial syllables are restricted to *a *ä *e *i *ə. Vowel harmony is probably early but its reconstruction is debated. Stress is initial.
phonotactics: Native roots are typically disyllabic: CVCV (e.g. *kala, *wete, *ńimi). Stem-final vowels (*-a *-ä *-e) are usual, and a few roots end in consonants. Word-initial consonant clusters are absent, and a word begins with a single consonant or a vowel. Medial clusters are permitted, mostly sonorant + stop, nasal + stop, or *ks *kt *lk *nt *mp (e.g. *ńelä, *kunta). No long vowels and no geminate consonants in the reconstruction.
orthography: Latin transliteration in standard Uralic Phonetic style, simplified for game use: c for affricate, s for sibilant, ń ś ĺ for palatalised segments, ŋ for the velar nasal, ä ü ö for front vowels, ə for the reduced vowel. Reconstructed forms are marked with an asterisk in scholarly use. In-game names are written without the asterisk.
morphology: Agglutinative suffixing, with no prefixes. Nouns take case and number suffixes: *-t plural, *-m accusative, *-n genitive, *-k or *-j nominalisers, *-lA or *-nA locative and ablative-type markers. Verbs take derivational suffixes: *-ktA, *-ntA, *-ma, *-mA deverbal noun, *-jA agent noun (cf. Finnish -ja, Hungarian -ó). Possessive suffixes on nouns: *-m 'my', *-t 'thy', *-s 'his or her'. There are no noun classes or grammatical gender, and no articles. Reduplication is marginal.
compounding: Compounds are head-final: modifier + head, with the modifier bare or in the genitive. Typical forms: N + N (e.g. 'fish-lake' = lake with fish), with the head last. Genitive constructions are 'X-n Y' = 'Y of X', with the possessor first and no linker beyond *-n. Agent nouns are built by adding the agent suffix to a verb or noun stem, so 'Y-maker' = Y + verb stem + *-jA. Place names often take a locative or collective suffix, such as *-lA or *-ńa.
noun_phrase_order: Modifier before head (adjective + noun, possessor + possessed, numeral + noun); the head noun is last. The verb is final in the clause.

sources: Sammallahti, Pekka. 1988. Historical phonology of the Uralic languages. In The Uralic Languages, ed. Denis Sinor
Janhunen, Juha. 1981. Uralilaisen kantakielen sanastosta. Journal de la Societe Finno-Ougrienne 77

notes: Speculative proxy. Proto-Uralic is not securely linked to Final Palaeolithic or Early Mesolithic foragers; the real languages of these populations are unknown and may be unrelated. Names should be built from Proto-Uralic-style roots as a plausible, internally consistent flavour only. No word may be identical to a Modern Irish, Scottish Gaelic or Manx word, since the language is not Goidelic. Current game strings (Cuhalak ninuk, Hilic silsi) violate the phonotactics: they use h, ch-like clusters and word-initial syllable shapes outside the reconstruction, and should be replaced with CVCV-based forms.
